subject: Operational insight — 2026-12-02 service disruption: summary & action timeline
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@lumenpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amanda Liu <amanda.liu@lumenpay.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Strange token delays this morning — request for timeline and next steps

Hi Karthik / Neha,

We saw pronounced token delays and a handful of 503s from 08:50–09:15 PST this morning; our dashboard shows a spike in tail latency for generation requests to model:gpt-small-4.

Impact: a small number of end-users experienced 10–20s response delays; ~0.4% of requests failed and auto-retried from our side. This is causing increased error logging and customer alerts.

Can you share what changed on your side, expected root cause, and immediate next steps? We need a short timeline to reconcile with our incident report and to provide a follow-up to our security team.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Platform Eng, LumenPay
jordan.price@lumenpay.com


From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@lumenpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Amanda Liu <amanda.liu@lumenpay.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Strange token delays this morning — request for timeline and next steps

Jordan — thanks for flagging this and apologies for the disruption.

Quick summary: our initial investigation shows a rollout of a kernel-selection optimization (deployed 08:45 PST) affected a small subset of long-prefixed sessions where KV cache pointers were misapplied after a model shard rotation. That led to longer-than-expected token generation times and a small number of session errors.

Immediate actions taken (high level):
- Rolled back the kernel-selection change at 09:05 PST (rollback completed by 09:12 PST).
- Enabled detailed tracing for session-state and KV cache hits across your tenant.
- Opened INF-4721 to track follow-up fixes and verification.

We're compiling a concise operational summary and an action timeline for you — I'll share a full note with the timeline, root cause, and required customer-side verification steps by EOD next Tuesday (Dec 9).

If you need interim artifacts (raw traces or request IDs) for your internal audit, tell me which format you prefer.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Site Reliability — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@lumenpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Amanda Liu <amanda.liu@lumenpay.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Operational insight — consolidated timeline, findings, and action items (attached)

Jordan / Amanda —

Attached is a concise operational insight packet that summarizes what happened on 2026-12-02, and the actions we will take to prevent recurrence. Attachments: inference-timeline.csv (event-level timestamps), config-diff.patch (rolled-back diff), post-incident-checklist.pdf (verification steps).

Executive summary (short):
- What happened: a targeted kernel-selection optimization was rolled to a 10% canary starting at 08:45 PST. For long sessions that had previously accumulated a non-contiguous KV cache due to a prior shard shuffle, the new kernel path did not validate a cached pointer; this caused occasional KV lookups to miss and forced a fallback path that incurred 8–18s extra latency and, in some cases, a session error leading to a 503 at the runtime layer.
- Scope & impact: affected ~0.4% of active requests across the region (us-west), producing tail-latency spikes and ~0.3–0.5% request failures for model:gpt-small-4 between 08:50–09:12 PST. No data leakage or unauthorized access observed.
- Mitigation & recovery: rollback at 09:05 PST; traffic rebalanced and retries cleared by 09:12 PST. Monitoring thresholds reverted and an automated rollback rule added for similar kernel regressions.

Detailed timeline (key events):
- 08:40 PST — Pre-rollout verification completed, canary scheduled.
- 08:45 PST — Kernel-selection optimization started (10% canary).
- 08:50 PST — First tail-latency alerts for affected shard set.
- 08:56 PST — Engineering investigation begins (traces show increased KV misses).
- 09:05 PST — Emergency rollback initiated.
- 09:12 PST — Rollback complete; error rates and latency return to baseline by 09:20 PST.

Root cause (concise):
- A code-path change to kernel selection removed a defensive KV-pointer validation in the canary build. In the common code-path the validation had been present; the regression only appeared in the new path and only for long-lived sessions with prior shard shuffle history.

Action items and owners (timeline):
1) Immediate (done): rollback and tracing enabled — Owner: SRE (Redwood) — Done 09:12 PST
2) 48–72 hrs: automated lint/regression gate to detect pointer-validation removal in kernel builds — Owner: Runtime team (Neha Kapoor) — ETA 2026-12-11
3) 1 week: targeted canary policy update to include session-history replay for long-lived sessions — Owner: Release Eng (Marissa Cole) — ETA 2026-12-16
4) 2 weeks: reconcile session-history and shard rotation tests in CI; add synthetic long-session load test — Owner: Runtime & QA — ETA 2026-12-23
5) 30 days: post-deployment verification run for your tenant (we will coordinate window) and delivery of verification report — Owner: SRE + Customer Success — ETA 2027-01-09

Customer verification steps (brief):
- We will schedule a 60-minute verification run during a mutually agreed maintenance window.
- Prior to that run we'll provide a short checklist (see attached post-incident-checklist.pdf) with log markers to validate that the corrected kernel path never exercises the fallback.

Data & compliance notes:
- No user data was exposed; traces shared will be redacted for PII.
- We can provide a scoped evidence package for your security team (traces, build hashes, deployment records).

Attachments: inference-timeline.csv (CSV: timestamp,event,shard,request_id), config-diff.patch (diff of the rolled-back change), post-incident-checklist.pdf (verification checklist).

If you'd like, we can present this to your security and platform teams next week (15–30 minute briefing). Suggested times: Tue 12/14 09:00–11:00 PST or Wed 12/15 13:00–15:00 PST.

Thanks again for your patience — we're treating this as high priority and will report completion against each action item above.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Site Reliability — Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0183
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Amanda Liu <amanda.liu@lumenpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@lumenpay.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational insight — consolidated timeline, findings, and action items (attached)

Thanks Karthik — that write-up is exactly what we needed. A few quick items:

1) We’d like the verification run to be scheduled the week of 2026-12-20; Tue 12/21 morning PST works best for our on-call.
2) Please redact all request IDs in anything shared externally, but we will request unredacted IDs under an NDA if required for our internal forensics.
3) Could you add the build hash that was rolled back to the event CSV (INF-4721)? We will reference that in our internal report.

If you can send a calendar invite for 12/21 09:00 PST for the verification window (tentative), that would help. Appreciate the clarity and the timeline — Amanda

Amanda Liu
Security Operations, LumenPay
amanda.liu@lumenpay.com
